newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-Australian Senate fails to amend budget bill.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-Australian Senate fails to amend budget bill.

text.p: The Australian Senate's two key Independent members backed the government on Wednesday in voting down an attempt to amend one of the biggest budget bills in the upper house.
Non-government senators had sought to eliminate the bill's measure to impose higher charges for some university courses.
Senate officials expect the upper house later on Wednesday to move onto the bill's other significant fiscal measure -- a lower income threshhold initiating repayment of student loans.
They expect the Senate to vote on the bill finally after that.
The bill, the Higher Education Amendment Bill, is part of the government's fiscal tightening, which aims to cut A$7.2 billion from the budget next fiscal year, from July.

Of that total tightening, about A$2 billion is in doubt because of opposition from non-government parties, forcing the government to rely on the doubtful support of the two Independents, Brian Harradine and Mal Colston.
This bill is worth about A$300 million to the 1997/98 budget.
